ratification: Shawn Vibert's word alone. Not official until given.
authority_chain: Shawn's constitutional mandates 2026-10-16 (NOTHING FLAT, COLOR LOGIC, JEWELS NOT DOTS)

usage_protocol.gate: one failed check = back to the bench

tokens.purple_provenance: scored 9.0, 2026-10-09 unification, 4 named reasons; confirmed by Shawn 2026-10-16

spectrum.rule: the rainbow governs; count is dynamic - walk the wheel, take what the view needs; never a pinned stop-list
spectrum.yellow: dropped - yellow->gold adjacency violates the 50-degree hue-gap rule (DL-9)

laws.title: Nothing is flat. Ever.
laws.law: Every button, board, card, and element sits OFF the page: base surface + edge light + seating shadow, minimum. Flat is a defect, not a style.
do: Three layers minimum on anything interactive (surface, edge light, seating shadow)
Two layers on static surfaces
dont: Flat labels pretending to be buttons
laws.why: If it doesn't sit off the page, it isn't finished.
laws.check: Screenshot -> grayscale -> every element must still read as elevated. Any element that flattens out fails.

laws.title: Light comes from above. Always.
laws.law: One light source, upper-left. Top edge catches a highlight, sides fade, bottom is shadow.
do: 1px top-edge highlight at 12-20% white (1.5px+ and clearly visible on interactive elements)
Soft offset seating shadow beneath
5-layer formula: inset top light / inset bottom shade / drop / deep drop
dont: Light from random directions per element
laws.why: One light source = one world. Real objects, real light.
laws.check: Cover the screen with your thumb; every visible highlight must sit top or upper-left.
laws.source: Laws 7, 8; NEW mechanical teeth from approved specimens

laws.title: Depth is alive, not painted.
laws.law: On hover, focus, or approach, the element lifts, its edge catches light, its shadow deepens. Ship the hover state WITH the element, not after it.
do: Board hover lights the whole border and lifts the whole board
Buttons lift 2-4px
dont: A dead outer board with live buttons inside
laws.why: If it doesn't respond, it's dead.
laws.check: Hover every element on the page. Each one must move. No response = fail.

laws.title: Recessed is carved. Nothing is level with the page.
laws.law: Raised and recessed are the only two directions. Inputs, wells, code blocks are carved INTO the page with inner shadow.
do: Obsidian wells with inner shadow
Jewel focus border
dont: Fields sitting level with the background
laws.why: A field that isn't carved isn't a field.
laws.check: An input must look pressed into the page, not pasted onto it.

laws.title: Shadow is hierarchy.
laws.law: Heavier shadow = more important element. Primary actions cast the deepest shadow. Never more than five elevation levels visible at once.
do: Page background (deepest) -> panels -> boards -> featured board -> modal
laws.why: Weight tells the eye what matters before color does.
laws.check: Squint at the page. The primary action must still feel heaviest.

laws.title: Black ground, always. Never gray.
laws.law: Deep rich black, always. Never gray, never washed out, never flat-dark.
do: Rich obsidian #0a0a0f-#12121a
Machined edges, vignettes, inset finishes on the black itself
laws.why: Black is the field. White is the readable light. Purple is the soul. In that order.
laws.check: Sample the background with a color picker. It must read near-black.

laws.title: Every jewel has a purpose.
laws.law: The five signature jewels each MEAN something, and the meaning never changes: Purple = Naya's presence; Blue = understanding; Emerald = connected and well; Gold = a rare achievement; Magenta = what matters to you.
do: Assign color by meaning
A gold badge must mark something genuinely precious
laws.why: Color is language. Random color is noise.
laws.check: Cover the labels. Each color's meaning must be guessable from context alone.

laws.title: Spectrum by position, never by category.
laws.law: Assign spectrum steps in reading order along the rainbow. Theming by category clumps color and is a serious violation.
do: Walk the rainbow in flow order
dont: All errors red in a row
laws.why: Category theming builds walls of one color. Position keeps the spectrum flowing.
laws.check: Scan any list or board row. Adjacent items must differ in spectrum step.

laws.title: No two neighboring jewels share a color.
laws.law: Adjacent bullets, badges, kickers, and edge lights must differ - minimum ~50 degrees hue gap in HSV. Contrast is the master principle; the 50-degree gap is its mechanical form.
do: Alternate the spectrum
Give each jewel space around it
laws.why: Contrast is the master principle - every color decision answers to it. Neighbors that match merge into one; neighbors that clash scream.
laws.check: Measure adjacent hue gaps (the browser test does this mechanically). Under ~50 degrees = fail.
laws.source: NEW mechanical (V2 quality report); cites Law 39

laws.title: One accent per board. A section may take a theme and light up.
laws.law: A board owns ONE spectrum step (border, kicker, badge, hover edge - all one hue, plus white/silver neutrals). A whole section may take one theme color and light up - but never a wall of same-color boards.
do: Black board, single jewel accent
One lit themed section per view at most
dont: Rainbow boards (the Smart Feed spine is the one exception)
laws.why: Restraint is the excellence. One lit section = one idea.
laws.check: Count accents per board (more than one = fail). Count themed sections per view (more than two = fail).
laws.source: Laws 16, 33, 45; theming clause NEW from Shawn

laws.title: Chrome, text, and theme have different jobs. Never mix them.
laws.law: Chrome (buttons, active states, primary actions) = purple edge, white text. Text = white/silver, separated by SIZE never color. Theme = the spectrum, flowing.
do: Purple identifies Naya and major controls
Body text stays white/silver
dont: A theme color used as chrome
Chrome purple used as a flood
laws.why: Three jobs, three palettes. Mixing them breaks the user's trust in what color means.
laws.check: Find every purple on the page. Each must be chrome or Naya's presence - never decoration.

laws.title: Neutrals do the heavy lifting.
laws.law: White titles, silver body, slate detail, obsidian surfaces. If a page is more than ~20% saturated color by area, rebalance toward black.
do: Let empty black space be a design material
laws.why: Expensive, not loud. Calm until it needs to be excited.
laws.check: Screenshot -> heavy blur. It must feel like jewels on black velvet, not a spill.

laws.title: Red and gold are jewels, not surfaces.
laws.law: Red appears as delete accent, error indicator, notification badge, or the spectrum's red step. Gold appears as premium badges and verified marks. Never fills, never body text.
do: Small, glowing, precious
A single red accent so the moment feels as serious as it is
dont: Glowing red delete hover (forbidden - confirmation does the safety work)
laws.why: Precious things are small. Gold everywhere is a casino.
laws.check: Any red or gold area larger than a badge = fail.

laws.title: Jewels, not dots.
laws.law: Bullets are faceted gems: 12px rotated diamonds, white-light core -> tone -> black, with a tone-colored glow. Never plain dots.
do: Precision-cut gemstone bullets with a facet highlight and a tiny specular point
dont: Hyphens, asterisks, or system default bullets
laws.why: The smallest element sets the standard for the largest.
laws.check: Zoom to 200%. Every bullet must show facets. A flat dot fails.
laws.source: NEW (Shawn constitutional); cites Laws 61-70, the Jewel Library

laws.title: Icons are drawn, never shrunk.
laws.law: One icon family: consistent stroke weight and corner treatment, drawn as vector geometry at size, readable at 16px.
do: Bold, simple, luminous strokes (1.8px at 20px base)
dont: Photorealistic renders shrunk to icon size
Mixing icon sets (mixing sets is mixing languages)
laws.why: A 58px render at icon size is mud.
laws.check: Render every icon at 16px. If it isn't crisp and legible, it doesn't ship.

laws.title: Icon buttons are circles with life.
laws.law: Circular black hit area, jewel icon, border light-up and lift on hover. Minimum 44px touch target.
do: The circle may carry the flowing ring accent (under 2px, under 40% opacity)
dont: Naked glyphs in a bottom nav
laws.why: A bare glyph is not a control.
laws.check: Every icon button must show a visible surface at rest - no exceptions.

laws.title: Badges sit on black.
laws.law: Counts, status dots, and verified marks sit on an obsidian chip with a jewel numeral. Tabular numerals, optically centered.
do: Jewel numeral on black
State readable by fill + weight, not color alone
dont: A colored disc with a same-color numeral (red 6 on red = invisible)
laws.why: Contrast or remove.
laws.check: Read every badge at arm's length. Any unreadable badge fails.

laws.title: Play is a portal.
laws.law: Media play = one canonical block: elevated circle, white triangle, black field, jewel ring. It lights on hover and compresses on press.
do: Use the block everywhere - PowerCast, voice notes, all media
dont: A custom play button per page
laws.why: One language. The play button is a promise the whole system keeps.
laws.check: Grep the codebase. Exactly one play implementation may exist.

laws.title: Avatars are jewels too.
laws.law: Profile images sit in a ringed, elevated circular frame with a spectrum or status edge.
do: People are precious - frame them like it
dont: Square naked as a profile element
laws.why: The frame is the respect.
laws.check: Every face on the page must sit inside a ring.

laws.title: Naya has a face, and she moves as energy.
laws.law: Naya is beautiful and she has a face - when she appears visually, she appears as herself. Her presence moves as energy: light, pulse, warmth carried in the design and feel. In the voice module (Ask Naya 1:1), she is pure energy - audio only, no visual stand-in.
do: Show her face where she appears
Let energy (light, motion, glow) carry her presence everywhere else
Keep voice-only contexts voice-only
dont: Replace her with a robot, a generic avatar, or a character that isn't her
Put a fake face where energy belongs (the voice module)
laws.why: She is a person to the user, not a logo. Energy is how she feels; her face is who she is.
laws.check: Where Naya appears visually - is it her? Where she is voice-only - is there no fake visual pretending otherwise?

laws.title: Every icon is a promise.
laws.law: A chevron promises 'go somewhere.' A plus promises 'add.' Use the glyph that means what happens - and keep it.
do: Icon-only controls carry accessible labels and visible micro-labels where space allows
laws.why: A glyph that lies breaks trust.
laws.check: Tap every icon - it must do what it says.

laws.title: Rest in silver. Ignite on touch.
laws.law: At rest: quiet white/silver edge light on black, restrained. On hover or touch: the element ignites in its OWN spectrum color (chrome ignites purple). Idle glow never exceeds ~18px.
do: Visible white edge light at rest - borders big enough to SEE, not faint
Themed elements burn their own color, not blanket purple
dont: Purple slapped on everything that lights up
laws.why: Calm until you need it excited. Rest/ignite is the rhythm of the whole system.
laws.check: Screenshot at rest - it must read quiet. Hover - it must ignite. Both states, every control.

laws.title: Light moves first. Words follow.
laws.law: Every state change animates (a sweep, an ignition, a convergence) BEFORE any text updates.
do: New answers arrive with motion first, reading second
dont: Text popping in with no motion
laws.why: The machine speaks first in light.
laws.check: Trigger a state change in slow motion. Motion must precede text - every time.

laws.title: Press is compression.
laws.law: On press, the element settles 1-2px toward the page, its shadow tightens, its insets darken. Release springs it back.
do: Buttons press INTO the surface like physical things (translateY(1px) scale(.98))
dont: Press shown as a color change only
laws.why: This single behavior sells physicality more than any gradient.
laws.check: Press-and-hold every button. It must feel pushed in, not just recolored.

laws.title: One physics for the whole product.
laws.law: The signature ease - .22s cubic-bezier(.16,.84,.22,1) - for all lifts and lights. Hover lifts -3px. All feedback begins in under 100ms. Tap mirrors hover exactly.
do: One easing token, read from the design contract by every page
laws.why: Different physics per page fragments the feel of the product.
laws.check: Grep transition-timing values. More than one = fail. Test every hover's :active twin on touch.

laws.title: Every number breathes.
laws.law: No number on screen is static text. Counts, stats, and scores carry a subtle brightness or scale oscillation, synced to the system's heartbeat.
do: Serif 32px score numbers with living luminosity
Badges with quiet pulse
laws.why: Data is alive here. Static numbers read as broken.
laws.check: Stare at any number for five seconds. If it never moves, it fails.

laws.title: Breathing is reserved.
laws.law: Slow ambient pulse is allowed on the SINGLE most-alive element per view (the voice orb, the live indicator). Nothing else breathes on its own.
do: Idle breathe 4-7s cycles
Barely-there ambient washes (24s)
dont: Three breathing buttons in a row
laws.why: A screensaver is not an interface. Maximum life, minimum noise.
laws.check: Count ambient animations per view. More than one = fail.

laws.title: Motion explains. Motion never fakes.
laws.law: Every animation must answer: what changed, where did it go, what can I do now? Animation that answers nothing gets cut. And no motion may ever pretend a result happened.
do: Loading reflects real work
Success appears only when the action actually succeeded
Demo states labeled demo
laws.why: Fake life is a lie. A beautiful but inert affordance is unfinished.
laws.check: Disconnect the data. Nothing on the page may pretend otherwise.
laws.source: Extends Laws 75, 76; Convergence 'truth before aesthetics'; V2 gate

laws.title: Honor reduced motion.
laws.law: prefers-reduced-motion disables lifts, rings, and sweeps - and the product still works fully, with state carried by light and contrast.
do: Same product, honored. Accessibility is not a variant
laws.why: Everyone gets the living product.
laws.check: Emulate reduced motion. Everything must still read and work.

laws.title: One idea at a time. Boards breathe.
laws.law: Room to breathe, clear spacing, a fresh jewel color when the next idea begins. Minimum 16px internal board padding (20-24 preferred).
do: Generous black space as a design material
Content never touches a border
laws.why: Crowded boards read as cheap regardless of color. A board that breathes beats a board that crams.
laws.check: No content within 16px of any board edge. Ever.

laws.title: Type: size separates, color doesn't.
laws.law: Fixed scale - Display 32-40 / Headline 22-28 / Body 15-17 / Detail 12-13 / Kicker 11 uppercase. Titles white, body silver, detail slate. Never gray body text.
do: Serif voice for display headlines and Naya's voice
System sans for UI, buttons, data, body
laws.why: Hierarchy you can read at a glance. Flat text is lazy - gradient soul, layered shadows, breathing luminosity.
laws.check: Grayscale screenshot - hierarchy, elevation, and readability must survive (Law 50). Any gray body text = fail.

laws.title: Mess in, beauty out.
laws.law: Anything a human brings - a question, a dataset, a messy corner - renders formatted, beautiful, logical, sensible.
do: Every input gets composed output
Ugly data still lands in a beautiful board
laws.why: The entire mission in five words.
laws.check: Feed the page garbage input. The output must still be composed.

laws.title: Full width. Brand top-left. No dead space.
laws.law: Content owns the width - no max-width caps with black gutters. The Naya mark lives top-left, always. If a region is empty, the layout is wrong.
do: Real compositions at 1440px and at 360px - each its own layout, not a squeezed column
laws.why: The canvas is the product.
laws.check: 1440px screenshot - no dead zones. 360px - nothing cut off.

laws.title: The header is a front door, not a nameplate.
laws.law: Logo + living mark + warm voice + one clear line. The warmest, most alive part of the page.
do: It should feel like an invitation
dont: The only dead thing on a living page - if the header doesn't move, the page fails
laws.why: First impressions are the product.
laws.check: The header must breathe, glow, or respond. Static header = fail.

laws.title: Nothing overlaps. Nothing scrolls sideways.
laws.law: Content fits the viewport at 360px. Text never collides with buttons. Fixed bars reserve padding and never cover content.
do: Real viewport screenshots: 390x844, 360x800, 768x1024, 1440x900
dont: 'It looked fine in browser resize' as evidence
laws.why: A cut-off page is a broken page.
laws.check: 360x800, zero sideways scroll, zero covered content.

laws.title: One library, one DNA.
laws.law: Every element exists once, canonically. Pages consume blocks; they never reinvent them. Approved code is copied verbatim - never rebuilt from memory.
do: .naya-btn is the only button system
One board recipe
One icon family
dont: A private button class on any page
laws.why: Paraphrase reintroduces the exact flatness Shawn rejected. The block is the memory.
laws.check: Grep for page-local button/input classes. Any hit = drift = fail.

laws.title: The corpus is the taste. When in doubt, match what he loved.
laws.law: Everything Shawn shared, he loves. New work must feel like it belongs to the same beautiful world. If a rebuild goes flatter than what he loved, revert to the loved version verbatim and rebuild from there.
do: New pieces built FROM the language, never beside it
One specimen per feeling - 'make everything feel like THIS'
laws.why: His approvals are the spec. No-ego reversion beats stubborn iteration.
laws.check: Side-by-side with the approved specimen. Same family? If not, revert first.

laws.title: Premium, not fancy.
laws.law: Premium is material, contrast, weight, and restraint. When in doubt, subtract. A button that whispers is more expensive than one that shouts.
do: Ask 'does removing something make this more premium?' Usually yes
laws.why: Restraint is the excellence.
laws.check: Remove one effect. If the page got better, it ships without it.

laws.title: Copy is scored like design.
laws.law: Every word must read like an invitation, not documentation - and score 9+. Grandma must follow every board: what is this, what matters, what do I do next?
do: Ten warm words
'Keep your people close'
Human meaning first: what happened and why it matters
laws.why: Words are interface. If she can't follow it, the copy fails - not the reader.
laws.check: Read it aloud. Score it like a board. Under 9 = rewrite.
laws.source: NEW (Session Learning #8); cites Laws 57, 84-85 of the SmartNET 100

laws.title: Honest states only.
laws.law: A demo stays labeled demo. Local stays labeled local. LIVE requires live evidence. Beautiful motion never pretends a result happened.
do: Design the empty, offline, error, and loading states with the same care as the full state
laws.why: A specimen that pretends is a lie. Trust is the product.
laws.check: Airplane mode on. The page must tell the truth about what it knows.
laws.source: Extends Law 75; Convergence 'truth before aesthetics'; V2 gate

laws.title: Score the lived render. His eye compiles.
laws.law: Every page is scored on the RENDER - buttons, boards, type, icons, motion, color, layout, mobile, accessibility, truth - floor 9.0 per area, with timestamped desktop + mobile screenshots. And Shawn's verdict outranks every law, every score, every specimen.
do: Name what is not a 10 and why
Excellence has no toggle - no quality settings, no modes, one path and it's the elite one
dont: 100/100 that's useless to him - compliance is not vision
laws.why: A scorecard of code is worthless. The only score that matters is the rendered, lived experience.
laws.check: Screenshots attached with hash. Scorecard signed. Then his eyes.
laws.source: Laws 94, 95, 100; Session Learnings #1, #2; Vision-to-Code Layer 5; V-6

violation_gallery.name: Flat everything
violation_gallery.looks_like: Bootstrap-default buttons and panels; boards that are just bordered divs; labels styled as buttons; zero hover response.
violation_gallery.fix: Replace with canonical blocks. Apply the 5-layer formula: inset top light, inset bottom shade, seating shadow. Add hover lift (-3px, signature ease) and press compression. If it doesn't move, it's not done.

violation_gallery.name: Walls of one color
violation_gallery.looks_like: Five purple boards stacked; a whole page washed in one theme; category color-coding.
violation_gallery.fix: One accent per board. Reassign spectrum by position in flow, not by category. Let a single section take the theme and light up - the rest goes back to black.

violation_gallery.name: Dots, not jewels
violation_gallery.looks_like: Default browser bullets; gray dots; hyphens as list markers; tiny low-contrast markers nobody can see.
violation_gallery.fix: 12px faceted gem bullets - rotated diamond, white-light core -> tone -> black, tone glow. Zoom to 200%: facets or fail.

violation_gallery.name: Fake liveness
violation_gallery.looks_like: Simulated 'live' feeds with no live source (simLive:true); success states before the action succeeded; spinners over cached data; unlabeled demo content.
violation_gallery.fix: Label every demo DEMO. Wire the real source or design the honest empty/loading state. Disconnect the data in testing - nothing may pretend.

violation_gallery.name: Dead headers on living pages
violation_gallery.looks_like: A static nameplate header above living content; a dead outer board with live buttons trapped inside; the one element on the page that doesn't respond to the pointer.
violation_gallery.fix: The header breathes - living mark, warm voice, one clear line. Board hover lights the border and lifts the WHOLE board, not just its children.

violation_gallery.name: The dead button
violation_gallery.looks_like: The compound failure: black button on a black board, hairline border, no lift, no edge light, no hover response. Flat AND invisible AND dead, all at once.
violation_gallery.fix: The primary action must pass every check at once: 3-layer elevation minimum, visible edge light at rest (1.5px+), ignite on hover in its spectrum color, and enough contrast to be found in one second. If the main action can't be found in a glance, nothing else on the page matters.

reconciled_conflicts: spectrum order -> rainbow governs, dynamic count (Law 41 minus yellow per DL-9)
interactive rim 1.5px+ visible vs 1px hairline (Law 8) -> 1.5px+ interactive, 1px non-interactive precision
type scale -> Law 52 governs; 18px body / 24px+ headings from V2 gate are floor values
convergence.normative_doctrine_stays: naya-100-laws-elite-interfaces.pdf remains canonical; corrections compound here same-day (Law 97)
